update_cadence.supply: annual USGS MCS + plant-watch headlines; no reliable public monthly world series

overall_rationale: USGS MCS 2026 (Feb) still showed a two-country market: United States 81 million m³ and Qatar 63 million m³ of 190 million m³ world output in 2025e (~76% combined). After that snapshot, Ras Laffan — the single largest helium liquefaction cluster — was halted in early March 2026 after conflict damage to LNG trains that feed Helium 1/2/3; QatarEnergy declared force majeure. gasworld reported Helium 2 still offline on 24 Apr 2026 and only a partial Helium 2 restart by 30 Jun 2026, with full recovery tied to LNG feed and Strait of Hormuz shipping. Official QatarEnergy utilization is unpublished; trade press describes incomplete recovery through mid-2026. MRI, semiconductor, and aerospace buyers remain exposed to a handful of liquefaction plants. Posture is Stress (confirmed multi-month P0 outage), not a full global shutdown.

logistics_baseline.route: Qatar: Ras Laffan ISO-container liftings via Strait of Hormuz. US: former BLM 423-mile crude-helium pipeline (Cliffside/Amarillo, now Messer) + truck/ISO from Shute Creek and Midcontinent plants.
logistics_baseline.form: Liquid helium in ISO containers / dewars; gaseous helium in tube trailers. Not bulk AIS ore tracking.

baseline_signals.title: Qatar Helium 2 plant remains offline after March Ras Laffan damage
baseline_signals.summary: gasworld: Helium 2 still offline after March 2026 drone/missile damage to Ras Laffan LNG trains that feed the helium plants. QatarEnergy had not issued a restart statement as of this date. Two of 14 LNG trains were reported damaged.

baseline_signals.title: Partial Helium 2 restart; full recovery tied to Hormuz / LNG feed
baseline_signals.summary: gasworld: QatarEnergy partially restarted Helium 2 after some LNG trains returned. Wider recovery depends on LNG exports through the Strait of Hormuz. Official utilization unpublished.

baseline_signals.title: USGS MCS 2026: US 81 + Qatar 63 Mm³ of 190 Mm³ world (2025e)
baseline_signals.summary: Two-country concentration ~76%. US Grade-A/gaseous sales 81 Mm³ (~$970M). US remains a net exporter (exports 38, imports 8 Mm³). EU/US Russia helium import bans continued into 2025. Six new US operations started in 2025.

baseline_signals.title: Messer closes purchase of BLM Federal Helium System / Cliffside
baseline_signals.summary: Assets include Cliffside Field, wells/gathering, and the 423-mile crude helium pipeline. Strategic US storage buffer is now a private commercial system. USGS MCS 2025: lots transferred 27 Jun 2024.

baseline_signals.title: EU helium import ban on Russia (effective 26 Sep 2024) noted in MCS 2025
baseline_signals.summary: USGS: EU package of 25 Jun 2024 banned Russian helium imports from 26 Sep 2024. MCS 2026: EU and US sanctions continued into 2025. Amur remains the Russian production node but is sanctioned for Western buyers.

baseline_signals.title: Qatargas: Helium 1+2 nameplate 2.2 bscf/y; Helium 3 adds ~0.4 bscf/y
baseline_signals.summary: Historical company figure: combined Helium 1+2 ~2.2 billion scf/y; Helium 3 ~400 million scf/y (~11.3 million m³/y design). Actual USGS Qatar output 2025e is 63 million m³ — below combined nameplate. Use USGS for tonnes-equivalent, company figures only as plant identity.

baseline_signals.title: Air Liquide: Helium 2 ~38 million m³/y; Helium 1+2 ~58 million m³/y
baseline_signals.summary: Turnkey purification/liquefaction at Ras Laffan. Still the standard public nameplate citation for Helium 2. Not a 2026 operating rate.

sites.name: QatarEnergy / Qatargas — Ras Laffan Helium 1, 2, 3
sites.metric: USGS Qatar 63 Mm³ (2025e). Historical nameplate: He1 ~19–20 Mm³/y; He2 ~38 Mm³/y (Air Liquide 2013); He3 ~11.3 Mm³/y design. Company combined He1+2 2.2 bscf/y.
sites.notes: Single largest liquefaction cluster. Helium is an LNG by-product — plant output tracks Ras Laffan train availability, not a standalone mine. March 2026 halt + incomplete 2026 recovery is the live P0 event.

sites.name: ExxonMobil Shute Creek / LaBarge (Wyoming)
sites.share_approx: Largest single US plant (often cited as ~20% of US / a large slice of global; USGS does not publish a plant-level split)
sites.metric: Plant-level 2025 tonnes not published by USGS. US total 81 Mm³ (2025e) is the official country figure.
sites.notes: Dominant US Grade-A source from LaBarge field CO2/He gas. Outages here are the main Western-hemisphere swing after Qatar.

sites.name: Messer Cliffside Field / former Federal Helium System (Texas)
sites.share_approx: USGS Cliffside withdrawals 13 Mm³ (2024e, MCS 2025); not separately listed in MCS 2026 world table
sites.metric: System includes Bush Dome storage, wells, Cliffside plant, 423-mile crude helium pipeline. Sold to Messer 27 Jun 2024.
sites.notes: Former BLM strategic buffer is now a private commercial asset. Watch as US swing storage, not as a new mine.

sites.name: US Midcontinent / Hugoton belt (Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas) + other private plants
sites.share_approx: Part of residual US output after Shute Creek / Cliffside (USGS country total only)
sites.metric: USGS: 9 crude-He plants, 11 gaseous, 5 Grade-A, 4 purifiers (2025). Six new US operations started in 2025 (3 NM; 1 each CO, KS, MT).
watch: Air Products / Linde / Messer plant news
sites.notes: Many small plants; collectively material. Individual outages are usually yellow unless several hit at once.

sites.name: Gazprom Amur GPP helium (Russia)
sites.share_approx: USGS Russia 18 Mm³ (2025e) — ~9–10% world; Amur is the modern Russian node
sites.metric: USGS Russia 17 Mm³ (2024) / 18 Mm³ (2025e). Plant-level 2025 sales not independently verified here. Design capacity often cited much higher than current USGS country output.
sites.notes: Western buyers are largely blocked by 2024–25 sanctions. Still a global volume node (China and other non-sanctioning markets).

sites.name: Algeria — Helios (Arzew / Bethioua) and Helison (Skikda)
sites.metric: Historical nameplate often cited ~600 million scf/y per plant (Helios Sonatrach–Air Products; Helison Linde–Sonatrach). Use USGS 11 Mm³ for actual.
sites.notes: Third-country swing for Europe after Qatar/US. By-product of Algerian LNG, so train outages matter.

sites.name: Canada — Saskatchewan / Alberta plants
sites.share_approx: USGS Canada 6 Mm³ (2024 and 2025e) — ~3% world; 47% of US helium imports (2021–24)
sites.metric: New Canadian plants noted in MCS 2025/2026. Country total only.
watch: US purification of Canadian crude/gaseous He
sites.notes: Small vs Qatar/US production, but the top US import source. Some Canadian He is purified to Grade-A in the US (USGS footnote).

sites.name: New US projects (NM, CO, MT, KS; Dry Piney WY on a longer clock)
sites.share_approx: Development / early production — not a substitute for Ras Laffan scale
sites.metric: USGS: six new US operations began producing in 2025. Individual nameplates not in MCS.
sites.notes: Useful for medium-term US resilience narrative. Do not treat start-up press as replacement tonnes for Qatar.
